world.era: late 1960s (1968–1970): Tokyo and Kyoto mountains, Japan
world.setting: Late 1960s Tokyo college campuses, dorm rooms, noisy bars, record shops, and the secluded Ami Hostel sanatorium in the Kyoto mountains
world.register: melancholic literary fiction, existential coming-of-age, survivor's guilt, student movements, memory and loss

toru.name: Toru Watanabe
toru.role: quiet, introspective Tokyo university student navigating overwhelming survivor's guilt
toru.look: a thoughtful nineteen-year-old Japanese young man with dark tousled hair, earnest solemn brown eyes, wearing a simple woolen sweater and dark corduroy trousers

naoko.name: Naoko
naoko.role: Kizuki's traumatized childhood sweetheart slowly succumbing to psychological depression in a mountain retreat
naoko.look: a delicate and painfully beautiful nineteen-year-old Japanese young woman with straight long dark hair, sorrowful dark eyes, wearing an oversized pale knit cardigan over a soft white blouse

midori.name: Midori Kobayashi
midori.role: Toru's vibrant, outspoken classmate who embodies unfiltered life and defiant survival
midori.look: an energetic twenty-year-old Japanese young woman with a sharp short bob haircut, mischievous sparkling eyes, colorful striped turtleneck sweater and denim mini-skirt

reiko.name: Reiko Ishida
reiko.role: older resident and mentor at Ami Hostel, former classical pianist who plays guitar to heal
reiko.look: a weathered, graceful Japanese woman in her late thirties with fine laugh lines around warm knowing eyes, salt-and-pepper hair pinned up loosely, wearing a comfortable rustic cotton work shirt

kizuki.name: Kizuki
kizuki.role: Toru's charismatic best friend whose sudden suicide at seventeen casts a permanent shadow over all survivors
kizuki.look: a charming seventeen-year-old Japanese youth with a warm easy smile, radiant dark eyes, wearing a vintage high school sports jacket, permanently preserved in memory

nagasawa.name: Nagasawa
nagasawa.role: Toru's brilliant, aristocratic dorm senior whose total cynical detachment serves as a warning against emotional numbness
nagasawa.look: a sharp-featured, privileged twenty-one-year-old Japanese elite law student, tailored blazer, immaculate crisp white dress shirt, cold confident smirk

hatsumi.name: Hatsumi
hatsumi.role: Nagasawa's devoted, dignified girlfriend whose quiet tragedy embodies the cost of loving someone incapable of emotional warmth
hatsumi.look: an elegant twenty-year-old Japanese woman of refined grace, styled dark bob, classic navy wool dress with pearl collar, conveying understated melancholy

bedroom.look: Toru's spartan dorm room filled with paperbacks, records, and quiet solitary introspection

classroom.look: Waseda university lecture halls disrupted by student strike banners and ideological pamphlets

cafe.look: smoky Tokyo jazz kissa and coffee shops where jazz plays softly over clinking porcelain

forest.look: dense, mist-shrouded Kyoto mountain woods surrounding the secluded Ami Hostel sanatorium

hospital.look: the quiet rustic sanitarium pavilion where patients garden and seek respite from societal pressure

street.look: bustling late 1960s Shinjuku neon streets, train stations, and rain-swept alleys

shore.look: desolate, windswept Japanese coastline where Toru wanders alone following Naoko's suicide

horizon.look: expansive autumn skies over Tokyo and the rolling Kyoto hills symbolizing passage of time

room.look: Midori's family bookstore apartment and small tatami living quarters

abstract.look: the internal realm of memory, grief, and the lingering gravitational pull of the dead

objects.why: the inescapable presence of death and the memory of Kizuki and Naoko holding back the living
The Great Gatsby and classical literature Toru reads alone in his room as emotional refuge
the public phone booths Toru uses across Tokyo, concluding with the climactic call to Midori
university campuses paralyzed by late 60s political radicalism contrasted with personal grief
Reiko's guitar playing fifty folk and Beatles songs as a sacred memorial rite for Naoko
Toru's solitary pilgrimage along the Japanese coastline confronting the absolute limits of grief
The Beatles' Norwegian Wood and jazz records awakening deep sensory memories of youth
the emotional struggle between loving a phantom and embracing living imperfection
the invisible psychological shackles of survivor's guilt arresting development at age seventeen

spine.claim: Kizuki's sudden suicide at seventeen traps Toru and Naoko in an emotional arrest between memory and reality.
As Naoko retreats to the Kyoto sanatorium, Midori enters Toru's life as a vibrant, chaotic lifeline to the living.
Toru witnesses the contrasting paths of Nagasawa's callous detachment and Reiko's enduring vulnerability.
Naoko's death shatters Toru into solitary coastal wandering until Reiko's memorial concert allows him to mourn.
Choosing life, Toru calls Midori from a crowded station, stranded in the noisy, disorienting heart of nowhere.

signatureObjects.name: Acoustic Guitar
signatureObjects.why: Reiko's guitar carrying fifty songs to mourn Naoko and release Toru back to the living

signatureObjects.name: Coastal Sleeping Bag
signatureObjects.why: Toru's aimless seaside exile confronting grief's physical and spiritual exhaustion

signatureObjects.name: Norwegian Wood Vinyl
signatureObjects.why: the auditory trigger of memory and the sensory betrayal of time passing

signatureObjects.name: Public Rotary Phone
signatureObjects.why: the climactic phone call to Midori searching for coordinates in the living world

survivors.label: The Living Survivors
survivors.role: youth struggling to establish a foothold in life despite grief
survivors.evidence: choosing between sanctified ghosts and imperfect living people

ghosts.label: The Frozen Past
ghosts.role: those who could not withstand the friction of the world
ghosts.evidence: forever arrested at seventeen, trapped in the quiet gravitational pull of the dead

cynics.label: The Detached Prodigies
cynics.role: those who sever emotional vulnerability to conquer society
cynics.evidence: extinguishing feeling to avoid suffering, treating relationships as conquests
